extracted.intended_audience: SEC reporting professionals, preparers of financial statements for business combinations, auditors, and financial/legal advisors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on applying the SEC 'tests of significance' (income, asset, investment) for business acquisitions, dispositions, joint ventures, reverse acquisitions, and step acquisitions under Regulation S‑X/S‑K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test when fiscal year changed (transition period < nine months)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the most recently filed financial statements are for fewer than nine months due to a change in fiscal year, the registrant may either (a) use the audited financial statements for the previous year-end before the change, or (b) use a continuous 12-month period consisting of the audited transition period plus months from the audited fiscal year before the transition so a total of 12 months of operations is available (ending on the last day of the transition period). [FRM 2025.6]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If transition period is fewer than nine months, registrant has a choice of the two alternatives above. The continuous 12‑month period can be derived by combining the transition-period audited statements with months from the prior audited year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test when fiscal year changed (transition period nine months or more)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the transition period is nine months or more, the registrant must use the audited financial statements for the transition period because a period of nine to 12 months is considered equivalent to one year under S‑X Rule 3‑06. [FRM 2025.6]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the audited transition‑period financial statements as the basis for the income test when transition ≥ 9 months; see S‑X Rule 3‑06 for related requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test when both registrant and acquired business changed fiscal years
rubrics_metrics.description: If both changed fiscal years, the same choices as for a single change apply, but the registrant must use a consistent approach for both entities: either both entities' audited financial statements for the previous year-ends are used, or both audited 12‑month periods that include and end with their respective transition periods are used. If the audited transition period is nine months or more, that period must be used. [FRM 2025.6]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency across registrant and acquired business is required when both change year‑ends; treat the transition period length rules the same for each entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test when interim audited period voluntarily filed (fewer than 12 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: When financial statements cover fewer than 12 months because a registrant voluntarily filed an audited interim period, the income test is performed using the audited financial statements for the registrant’s most recently completed fiscal year on file. A registrant may use audited 12‑month periods that do not end on its fiscal year-end only when it obtains pre‑clearance through a written request to the SEC staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntarily filed audited interim periods (<12 months) are not used in place of the most recently completed fiscal year unless SEC pre‑clearance is obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test when entity existed fewer than 12 months
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant or the acquired business has existed fewer than 12 months, perform the income test based on the audited income statement available; it is inappropriate to annualize income from continuing operations. If one entity has a full year and the other does not, use each entity's most recently filed periods (do not adjust the full‑year entity to match months). [FRM 2025.5]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not annualize. If one party has <12 months and the other has 12 months, calculate pretax income component using the actual audited periods for each entity. Consider consulting legal counsel/SEC staff about whether the revenue component should apply when one party has <12 months of history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset test – definition and computation
rubrics_metrics.description: An acquisition is significant under the asset test if the registrant’s proportionate share of the acquired business’s consolidated total assets (after intercompany eliminations and before purchase accounting adjustments) exceeds 20% of the registrant’s consolidated total assets as of the end of the most recent fiscal year for which financial statements are required to be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute numerator = registrant’s proportionate interest (direct + indirect) in acquired business’s consolidated total assets (after eliminating intercompany). Denominator = registrant’s consolidated total assets per most recent annual financial statements required to be filed (exclude assets of the acquired business). If result > 20% → acquisition significant under asset test; if ≤ 20% → must still complete income and investment tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset test decision rule and next steps
rubrics_metrics.description: If the asset test result is greater than 20% the business acquisition is significant. If not, the registrant must complete the income test and the investment test to determine overall significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a decision flow: perform asset test first; >20% → file required SEC disclosures for significant acquisitions (see chapter 4); ≤20% → continue with other tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset test treatment of noncontrolling interest (NCI)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant acquires 100% of a business that presents NCI in its consolidated statements, use the total assets as reported on the acquired business's financial statements; do not adjust the numerator for the NCI holder's interest. If a registrant acquires less than 100% of a business, the numerator is the acquired business's total assets multiplied by the percentage acquired (no adjustment for NCI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This parallels guidance on the revenue component of the income test. Use reported total assets and multiply by acquired percentage when acquisition <100%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset test inclusion of working capital assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Working capital assets are included in the acquired business’s total assets for the asset test even if some working capital items (e.g., accounts receivable) are not acquired, because working capital is expected to be required and funded after acquisition. [FRM 2015.4]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assets other than working capital are excluded, registrant must assess whether excluded assets are 'normal and necessary' to operations; if so, they are likely included. These determinations require facts-and-circumstances judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset test exclusion of non‑operational assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Assets that are not working capital and are not necessary to operate the business after acquisition (e.g., life insurance cash surrender value, note receivable from selling shareholder) may be excluded from the acquired business's consolidated total assets for the asset test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEC staff has permitted exclusion of such items where they are not normal and necessary to operations; document facts and rationale for exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset test for acquisition of partnership interests
rubrics_metrics.description: When purchasing a general or limited partnership interest, determine the registrant's proportionate share of the acquired business's assets using the percentage ownership acquired. The SEC staff may require financial statements under S‑X Rule 3‑13 if the test results are extremely disproportionate relative to the overall effect on the acquirer's financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even small percentage acquisitions can lead to consolidation or disproportionate balance sheet effects; consider whether omission of acquired business financials would be material to investors and consult SEC staff as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset test for step (staged) acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant increases its existing investment in an entity (step acquisition), perform the asset test based on the additional interest acquired. Significance is determined as the increase in the registrant’s pro rata interest in the investee’s consolidated total assets over the registrant’s consolidated total assets. [FRM 2020.3]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the incremental percentage acquired is used in the numerator; prior holdings are not remeasured into the numerator for the asset test calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of remeasurement of previously held equity interest on obtaining control
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Topic 805, when an investor obtains control of an entity in which it previously held an interest, it remeasures its previously held equity interest to acquisition‑date fair value with recognition of gain or loss in earnings. That remeasurement is not included in the asset test because it is not included in the registrant's consolidated financial statements for its most recent fiscal year required to be filed before the acquisition. [FRM 2020.4]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include acquisition‑date remeasurement gains/losses in the numerator of the asset test; use asset amounts per the acquired business's financial statements at the applicable measurement date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reverse acquisitions – which historical financials to use
rubrics_metrics.description: After a reverse acquisition, the accounting acquirer’s historical financial statements are presented as the historical financial statements of the combined entity in post‑acquisition filings. The accounting acquirer’s historical financial statements and reporting history are used for testing significance under S‑X Rule 3‑05. [FRM 12210.1]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When testing significance for acquisitions made after a reverse acquisition but before filing the first post‑reverse-acquisition Form 10‑K (or otherwise), base tests on the accounting acquirer’s historical financials (i.e., the entity identified as the acquirer for accounting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test for dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: For dispositions, the investment test is performed by dividing the registrant’s investments in and advances received for the disposed business by the registrant’s AWMV (if available). For a disposition, the registrant’s investments in and advances received is the consideration received, including contingent consideration. [S‑X Rule 1‑02(w)(1)(i)(A)(2)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consideration received (not carrying value) as the numerator when applying the investment test to dispositions; include contingent consideration where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test when AWMV is not available
rubrics_metrics.description: If AWMV is not available for the registrant, the investment test is performed by dividing the carrying value of the disposed business by the registrant’s consolidated total assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fallback to carrying value/total assets as the investment‑test ratio when AWMV cannot be calculated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test in a spin‑off
rubrics_metrics.description: In a spin‑off, the investment test is performed by dividing the carrying value of the disposed business (or the portion disposed) by the registrant’s total assets as of the end of the most recent fiscal year prior to the disposal date. A registrant’s AWMV is not used in a spin‑off. [FRM 2130.2 (n 3), 2020 AICPA Conf]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use carrying values and prior fiscal‑year total assets for spin‑offs; do not use AWMV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretax income numerator for dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: For the disposition of a business, the numerator of the pretax income component of the income test is based on the income statement effects that would be removed from the registrant's income statement during the tested period (similar to discontinued operations presentation), not on pretax income calculated on a carve‑out basis under SAB Topic 1.B.1. [Regs Comm 10/2020]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When calculating the pretax income component for a disposition, identify the income that will be eliminated from the registrant's results in the tested period rather than constructing a carve‑out pretax income solely for the disposed entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint venture acquisitions and dispositions are within scope of S‑X Rule 3‑05
rubrics_metrics.description: The acquisition of an interest in a joint venture is considered the acquisition of a business (regardless of consideration exchanged) and is in scope of S‑X Rule 3‑05; determining significance for joint venture acquisitions and dispositions has unique challenges and must be addressed separately for acquisition and disposition portions. [Question 2.2.150]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat joint venture contributions as both an acquisition (equity method investment) and a disposition (business contributed) when each partner contributes a business; perform significance tests separately for each side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test for joint venture acquisition (when each partner contributes a business)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the acquisition portion, the investment test is based on the purchase price divided by the registrant’s AWMV, if available. The numerator may be the fair value of the consideration transferred to the other joint venture partner(s) or the fair value of the consideration received, whichever is more readily determinable. [FRM 2025.4]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the numerator (consideration transferred or received) that is more readily determinable; use AWMV as denominator when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test for joint venture acquisition (components and selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: The income test for the acquisition portion of a joint venture formation is determined based on the pretax income component or the revenue component, whichever yields the lower percentage. The pretax income component uses the registrant's share of the acquired business's pretax income divided by the registrant's consolidated pretax income. The revenue component (if applicable) uses the registrant's share of the acquired business's consolidated total revenue divided by the registrant's consolidated total revenue. If the registrant and the contributed business do not both have material recurring annual revenue in each of the two most recently completed fiscal years, only the pretax income component applies. [FRM 2025.4]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute both components where possible and use the lower result for the income test; if revenue history is not available for both parties for the two most recent years, rely only on pretax income component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset test for joint venture acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: The asset test for the acquisition portion of a joint venture formation is based on the registrant's share of the acquired business’s consolidated total assets (i.e., the registrant’s portion of assets contributed by other joint venture partner(s)) divided by the registrant’s consolidated total assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same asset‑test ratio mechanics as other acquisitions but use the registrant's proportional share of the partner‑contributed assets as the numerator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition portion of joint venture formation – tests performed on percentage disposed
rubrics_metrics.description: For the disposition portion of a joint venture formation, the significance tests are performed in the same way as the acquisition portion but are based on the percentage of the business disposed (not 100% of the business contributed). [Regs Comm 03/2011]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For dispositions resulting from contribution to a joint venture, use the portion disposed as the basis for numerator calculations in investment, asset, and income tests.
